title: Lead with 'one-time purchase, no subscription'
rationale: DaisyDisk ($9.99) and Mole ($19) explicitly sell one-time with no subscription, while CleanMyMac, MacCleaner Pro, Hyperspace and Sensei all pair a one-time option with subscriptions. A plain no-subscription promise may stand out against the suite vendors, but DaisyDisk and Mole already own that message at the low end.

title: Price in the gap between $19 and ~$60-90 one-time
rationale: Verified one-time prices: DaisyDisk $9.99, Mole $19, Sensei $59, Hyperspace lifetime $49.99, MacCleaner Pro $85.95, CleanMyMac $89.99 (App Store price). There is a populated low tier and a populated suite tier; a price around $29-$49 for a full cleanup-plus-uninstaller app may read as fuller than Mole but cheaper than the suites.

title: Combine cleanup, uninstaller and disk map in one native app
rationale: Most verified products cover one or two of these: AppCleaner and Pearcleaner uninstall, DaisyDisk and GrandPerspective visualize. Only Mole was verified covering cleanup, uninstall and a disk map together, at $19. A bundle priced above Mole but with a stronger story could be viable; Mole is the closest direct threat.

title: Offer a free scan-first trial rather than a short timed trial
rationale: Hyperspace allows unlimited free scanning and Mole lets each paid tool run twice free, while MacCleaner Pro gives only a 2-day trial and CleanMyMac a 7-day trial. Showing reclaimable space before purchase may build trust in a category where users worry about deleting the wrong files.

title: Treat developer-tool cleanup as a feature to test, not yet a proven gap
rationale: Mole was verified covering developer-tool and build-output cleanup; for the other nine competitors the field is unknown because their pages do not mention it, which is not evidence they lack it. Before treating this as a differentiator, check the other competitors' docs and release notes in a follow-up run.
